messages.author: 9748b18016bf040c
messages.subject: converting a model to Stan
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to convert the following OpenBUGS code to Stan

model;
{
  p ~ dbeta(1,1)
  psi ~ dunif(0,1)

  for (i in 1:M) { 

    w[i] ~ dbern(psi)
    bp[i] <- w[i]*p
    caps[i] ~ dbin(bp[i],nDays)

  }
  N <- sum(w[1:M])
}

this is for a capture-recapture model (simplified here), with the basic idea being: we'll sample from a population of unknown size N, get a vector of the number of times some individuals were captured, augment this capture vector with a bunch of zeros so it's now of length M>N (we're choosing M large enough to ensure there are actually more zeros than unobserved individuals), then try to estimate the indicator variables w[i]'s which will be 1 if an individual belongs to the true population of size N.

for example: with N=5, nDays=20 if we capture n=3 tigers and get caps=c(3,1,1), then  M=10  gives the augmented data caps=c(3,1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0), and the OpenBUGS code gives:


one of the big things to notice here is the first 3 individuals were captured, and we have correctly estimated w[1]=w[2]=w[3]=1  with sd=0. Also since the rest of the w's corresponding to individuals without observations will oscillate between 0 and 1, we would expect these w's to end up close to  (M-n)/(M-N) = 0.4 

the following is my attempt to convert this to Stan:

functions{
  real binomZero_log(int y,int n, real p){
    real pdf;
    if(p==0){
      pdf = 0;
    }
    else{
      pdf = lchoose(n,y)+y*log(p)+(n-y)*log(1-p);
    }
    return pdf;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=0> nDays;
  int<lower=0> M;
  int<lower=0> caps[M];
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=1> psi;
  real<lower=0,upper=1> p;
  real<lower=0,upper=1> wr[M];
}

transformed parameters{
  real w[M];
  real N;
    for(i in 1:M){
    if(wr[i]<psi){
      w[i] = 1;
    }
    else{
      w[i] = 0;
    }
  }
  N = sum(w[1:M]);
}

model {
  psi ~ uniform(0, 1);
  p ~ beta(1,1);   
  wr ~ uniform(0,1);  
  for(i in 1:M){
    caps[i] ~ binomZero(nDays,w[i]*p);
  }
}


which for the same example as above gives much worse estimates and also is allowing the first three w's to be zero for some of the iterations


I believe I have to write the binomZero_log function, since I need the binomial prior to take a zero probability parameter, otherwise the w's wont get fixed at 1 (I did try this and that's the result I found but additionally for the full model I will sometimes pass a p=0 to the binomial prior for other reasons). I'm wondering if initializing the w's and N in the transformed parameter block as real valued could have a problem? I tried moving the w's to the model block and initializing them as int and then just calculating them afterwards using the wr estimates or in the generated quantities block but I seemed to get the same results. I also tried switching the condition to set the w's to 1 to include if the individual was observed before with if(wr[i]<psi || obs[i]==1)  , this of course gives the first 3 w's as 1, but doesn't result in the same outcome as the OpenBUGS for the rest of the w's or other parameters and doesn't seem to have any effect on the wr's (i've rewritten the OpenBUGS code to include wr's to check and their clearly effected by psi during each iteration when I plot the trace plots together, where as the wr's in my Stan model do not appear to be). 

I think my question here really boils down to: in OpenBUGS when I set  caps[i] ~ dbinom(w[i]*p,nDays) it automatically fixes w[i]=1 if caps[i]>0, so would there be a way to get a similar result in Stan? It seems there should be since as I mentioned when I use the built in binomial prior in Stan it ends up forcing all the w's to 1 since it won't allow p=0, but if so I just haven't been able to figure out what way to define each parameter in the correct block, or another trick for getting them to communicate in this way yet.

I'm really new to Stan so I'm sorry if my question is relying on OpenBUGS too much here, so far I've really liked what I've seen with Stan (great job to anyone on the team, just the ability to use conditional statements is greatly appreciated) and I'm planning on completely switching over if I can get this to work so any help would be greatly appreciated, thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] converting a model to Stan
parts:
It helps if you tell us which variables are known (data) in
BUGS programs.

You're in luck for just about any kind of ecology model you
want.

Hiroki Ito translated all of the Kery and Schaub BUGS book
on population ecology to Stan:

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/BPA

The basic CJS mark-recapture model is in the manual chapter on
marginalizing latent discrete parameters. And there's a case study
on occupancy models that I think is what you're trying to do with this
JAGS model:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/dorazio-royle-occupancy.html

As well as some examples of adding predictors in Fraenzi's book:

https://www.amazon.com/Bayesian-Analysis-Ecology-Linear-Models/dp/0128013702

Recently, we've gone through developing a movement HMM with predictors
on the mailing list with Ben Lambert.

- Bob
